messages:
raj_prodops: Hi team — seeing intermittent 403s hitting /v1/chat.generate since I rotated a service key yesterday. Two req ids I pulled from the client logs: req_9f3c2a1b and req_9f3c2a1c. Happening from our prod pool (k8s).

maya_support: Thanks — can you paste a minimal curl (redact the token) + the exact req id you want us to look at? Also give the time window (UTC).

raj_prodops: sure, redacted curl below (ran at 2026-03-14T22:12:10Z).
```
curl -v 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" 
  -H "X-Org-ID: org-foo" 
  -H "X-Project-ID: proj-bar" 
  -H "X-Request-Id: req_9f3c2a1b" 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat.generate
```
Response we get: HTTP/1.1 403
{"error":"insufficient_scope", "message":"token org claim mismatch: org=org-xyz" }

maya_support: ok that's helpful. Two quick asks: 1) run the same curl with -v and paste the raw response headers (we want the WWW-Authenticate header if present); 2) can you confirm whether the token was minted from the new service key (id) or still from the old key?

raj_prodops: I rotated the key yesterday (new id sk_live_7gH...). Our deploy updated the secret in k8s but maybe some pods still have the old secret cached — will check. Verbose headers:
```
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< Content-Type: application/json
< X-Request-Id: req_9f3c2a1b
< Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2026 22:12:10 GMT
< WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="redwood", error="insufficient_scope", error_description="signed claim mismatch: org != header"
```

liam_eng_oncall: fwiw we've seen this pattern when a servicekey is rotated but long-lived tokens / cached credentials on a sidecar or edge proxy keep being used. The token's "org" claim can still be the old org if minting service wasn't using the new binding. Could be cache or a mis-bound servicekey.

ana_security: @raj_prodops please also include the audit-log window (UTC +/- 2min) for when req_9f3c2a1b occurred — we need the token jti and the key id (kid) from the audit event. If you can share the audit entry ID we can trace KMS and IAM evals.

infra-bot: gateway.log: 2026-03-14T22:12:10Z req=req_9f3c2a1b method=POST path=/v1/chat.generate client=10.4.2.7 hdr_x_org_id=org-foo hdr_x_project_id=proj-bar token_claims={org:org-xyz, proj:proj-old} validation=failed reason="claim(org) != hdr_x_org_id"

raj_prodops: ah — that log makes it obvious. We rotated the key and updated org binding to org-foo, but tokens issued by our auth service still have org=org-xyz (old). Some pods were still running the old auth service image. I'll redeploy the auth service to force new tokens.

maya_support: great, please repro after redeploy and paste one req id. If it still fails, we can ask infra to invalidate token cache at the gateway and run a debug bundle. To collect a debug bundle: run the repro curl with X-Debug: 1 and include the X-Request-Id header, then send the req id + timeframe to us and we will pull gateway traces.

raj_prodops: redeployed auth service, minted a fresh token, ran curl (req_9f3c2a9) — success: HTTP/1.1 200 and payload returned.
```
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: application/json
< X-Request-Id: req_9f3c2a9
{"id":"resp_2a7", "choices": [...] }
```

liam_eng_oncall: nice, that aligns with cached credentials theory. For mitigation: 1) ensure rolling restart on services that cache tokens; 2) set a short TTL for cached service tokens; 3) add a health-check that fails if token claims mismatch expected org/project.

ana_security: follow up: please paste the audit log event id for the failed request so we can confirm the kid / KMS rotation timeline. We'll check that the rotated key wasn't used to sign old tokens.

raj_prodops: audit id is audit_20260314_221210_42. Sending to support via DM (redacted).

maya_support: thanks — glad this is resolved by redeploy. I'll keep the thread open for a day in case you see recurrence. Also recommended: after key rotation, run a short canary that mints and validates a token and calls a simple endpoint to catch these caches. :thumbsup:

raj_prodops: will do, thanks everyone. Closing for now unless we hit it again. :slightly_smiling_face:
